Activation messaging (memory_91) is the close second and stays queued.

I am spending verification on memory_86 and memory_31 rather than on memory_73 precisely because 73 still carries its caveat and 86/31 do not. Consolidated summaries preserve headline lifts and shed qualifiers; the fact that 73's harm survived compression suggests it was severe enough to be unmissable, while 86 and 31 read as uniformly positive in a way that is suspicious. What I need from the archive is whether those experiments measured anything downstream of activation at all — retention, paid conversion, lead quality, revenue per account — or only the top-of-funnel metric they report. Cutting signup fields plausibly trades qualified-lead signal (firmographics, routing data) for raw activation counts, which would inflate the very metric I am chasing while degrading qualified revenue. Standard experiment, not broad rollout: the supporting evidence may be thinner than its summary implies, and I will not scale a change to the acquisition funnel on unverified compressed claims. Guardrails on paid conversion rate, 90-day retention, and revenue per new account, not just completion and activation.
